GA resolutions are not a formal source of international law under Article 38(1) of the ICJ Statute, because they are generally non-binding recommendations. Their value is as a material source: they may enunciate or help crystallise statements of customary law, serving as evidence of opinio juris (as in *Nicaragua* and *Nuclear Weapons*). They do not always reflect customary law, since that depends on the content, the voting pattern and state practice.
